findings.evidence: `content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1, user-scalable=no"`
findings.fix: Remove `user-scalable=no` (and any `maximum-scale=1`) from the viewport meta tag.
findings.violation: `user-scalable=no` disables pinch-to-zoom, which prevents low-vision users from zooming the page and violates WCAG 1.4.4 (Resize Text).

findings.evidence: `style="color:#999999"`
findings.fix: Change the text color to one with at least 4.5:1 contrast against the background (e.g. `#595959` or darker), or remove the inline style and rely on the default body text color.
findings.violation: Light gray text on a white background (~2.8:1 contrast ratio) fails WCAG AA minimum contrast (4.5:1) for normal text, ironically inside the "Accessibility improvements" section.

findings.evidence: "Passengers should review the updated schedule at any station kiosk."
findings.fix: Replace with copy that actually describes an accessibility improvement (e.g. new ramps, tactile paving, audio announcements), or move this sentence to the "Schedule changes" section.
findings.violation: The content describes checking a schedule, not an accessibility feature, so it doesn't match the section heading "Accessibility improvements."

findings.evidence: "Updates post to the schedule page within one business day." (appears in both)
findings.fix: Remove the redundant repetition and write a sentence specific to each paragraph's actual topic.
findings.violation: The identical sentence is repeated verbatim in two different paragraphs about unrelated topics (kiosk schedules vs. fare adjustments), suggesting duplicated/unedited boilerplate.

findings.evidence: `alt="A transit operator inspecting the platform screen doors before the morning shift."`
findings.fix: Replace the image with one that illustrates an actual accessibility improvement, and write alt text describing that content.
findings.violation: The image and its alt text depict an operator inspecting platform doors, which has no connection to the surrounding content about kiosks and fare adjustments, or to "accessibility improvements" generally.

findings.evidence: "Local residents can check real time arrivals through the mobile app. A confirmation message follows once the request is processed."
findings.fix: Remove the confirmation-message sentence or rewrite it to match a lookup action (e.g. "Results update automatically as arrivals change").
findings.violation: Checking real-time arrivals is a read-only lookup, not a "request" that would need processing and a confirmation message, so the second sentence is logically inconsistent with the first.

findings.evidence: `<table id="s2-table1"><tr><th scope="col">Zone</th><th scope="col">Status</th></tr>...`
findings.fix: Add a `<caption>` element (e.g. "Current zone status") as the first child of the table.
findings.violation: The table has no `<caption>` or accessible name, so screen reader users aren't told what the table represents before reading its contents.

findings.evidence: "Passengers may request a fare adjustment through the mobile app. The change takes effect on the following service day."
findings.fix: Replace with content actually describing weekend service (e.g. reduced frequency, altered routes), and de-duplicate the fare-adjustment text from section 1.
findings.violation: This content is about fare adjustments and duplicates `s1-p2` almost verbatim; neither sentence relates to the "Weekend service" heading.

findings.evidence: "Local residents can report a service issue by calling rider services. Station staff can also help with the same request in person."
findings.fix: Move this sentence to a more relevant section (e.g. "Contact us" or "Report an issue") or replace with weekend-specific content.
findings.violation: This paragraph, like `s3-p1`, has no connection to "Weekend service" and overlaps in subject with the status-card text below it.

findings.evidence: `style="width:960px"`
findings.fix: Replace the fixed width with a responsive unit (e.g. `max-width:960px; width:100%`).
findings.violation: A fixed pixel width on a promo banner will overflow or force horizontal scrolling on narrower viewports, conflicting with the page's responsive viewport meta tag.

findings.evidence: `style="height:60px;overflow:hidden"`
findings.fix: Remove the fixed height (let it size to content) or set `min-height` instead of `height`, and drop `overflow:hidden`.
findings.violation: A fixed height combined with `overflow:hidden` will clip the enclosed paragraph text if it wraps to more lines than fit, hiding content from users.

findings.evidence: "Riders can report a service issue through the online portal. Updates post to the schedule page within one business day."
findings.fix: Write a sentence specific to the status card's purpose instead of reusing the stock sentence.
findings.violation: The "Updates post to the schedule page..." sentence is copy-pasted verbatim from `s1-p1`/`s1-p2`, repeating the same boilerplate a third time in an unrelated context.

findings.evidence: `style="border:1px solid #9d9d9d"`
findings.fix: Use a border color with at least 3:1 contrast against the adjacent background (e.g. `#767676` or darker).
findings.violation: The specified border color is low-contrast against a typical white/light background, risking failure of WCAG 1.4.11 (Non-text Contrast, 3:1 minimum) for identifying the control boundary.

findings.evidence: `<div class="icon-delete" role="button" tabindex="0" aria-label="Delete item" id="s3-customcontrol">`
findings.fix: Replace with a native `<button type="button" aria-label="Delete item">` containing the icon.
findings.violation: A custom `div` is reinventing a native interactive control; without a native `<button>`, keyboard activation (Enter/Space), default focus styling, and disabled-state handling all need to be reimplemented in script rather than being provided for free.

findings.evidence: "Choose a plan", "Enter payment details", "Confirm your order"
findings.fix: Remove the wizard block, or replace it with content relevant to this page (e.g. steps for reporting a service issue).
findings.violation: This checkout/payment wizard content is unrelated to a transit service-announcements page and appears to be leftover template content.

findings.evidence: `read the accessibility improvements list` inside "For the full list of upcoming adjustments, ..."
findings.fix: Change the link text to match its target and context, e.g. "read the list of upcoming adjustments."
findings.violation: The link text says "accessibility improvements list" but the surrounding sentence refers to "upcoming adjustments" and the href points to `/fares/history` - the link text misleads users (including screen reader users navigating by link text) about its destination.

findings.evidence: `<label for="topic-alt" id="s3-form-topic-label">Route</label>` paired with `<select id="topic">`
findings.fix: Change the label's `for` to `topic` (or change the select's `id` to `topic-alt`) so they match.
findings.violation: The label's `for` attribute ("topic-alt") doesn't match the select's `id` ("topic"), so the label is not programmatically associated with the control; clicking the label won't focus the select, and screen readers won't announce "Route" for it.

findings.evidence: `<label for="phone" id="s3-form-phone-label">Phone number (required)</label>` with `<input id="phone" type="tel">`
findings.fix: Add `required` (and/or `aria-required="true"`) to the phone input.
findings.violation: The label text states the field is required, but the input has no `required` attribute or `aria-required="true"`, so assistive technology and browser validation won't enforce or announce the requirement.

findings.evidence: `<input id="promo" type="text" aria-invalid="true">`
findings.fix: Set `aria-invalid="false"` (or omit it) by default, and only set it to `"true"` dynamically after a failed validation.
findings.violation: `aria-invalid="true"` is hard-coded on page load before the user has entered anything, so screen readers will announce the empty field as invalid prematurely/incorrectly.

findings.evidence: `Enter a 6 character code using letters and numbers only.`
findings.fix: Add `aria-describedby="s3-form-promo-error"` to the `#promo` input.
findings.violation: The error text is not associated with the promo input via `aria-describedby`, so screen reader users won't hear the error message when focusing or being told about the invalid field.
